principles.description: The runnable item text block occupies more page space than any supporting section. It is the reason the page exists.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: Set On action + One Target + Limitations in one mechanics block
Salvage-Plate Harness: mechanic callout with edge cases and limitations inline

principles.description: Each fact appears once. No section restates the item text. At the Table adds only non-obvious play consequences.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: Mechanics owns rules, Provenance owns origin — no overlap
Salvage-Plate Harness: Mechanics owns the crit-blunt rule, no At a Glance repeating it

principles.description: Edge cases and limitations live inside the item text block, not in separate sections.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: target size, fire/water refusal, catch-pole recovery all inside Mechanics
Salvage-Plate Harness: downed wearer, spell-save crits, no-smith-tools all inside Mechanics

principles.description: Classification line immediately precedes the item text. No intervening sections.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: 'Tool (Trained Animal), Uncommon.' then straight into Mechanics
Salvage-Plate Harness: 'Armor (Harness), Uncommon.' then field table then Mechanics

principles.description: A DM reading only the item text block can run the item at the table without a design diary, comparator matrix, or balance commentary.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: +4 to hit, 1d8, DC 14, action to call off — all present
Salvage-Plate Harness: first crit per short rest, 10 min repair, action to don/doff — all present

principles.description: Provenance is 1–2 sentences when it changes play or establishes who made/sold it. Absent when it doesn't matter.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: one sentence naming Zort and the Mid-Chain contact
Salvage-Plate Harness: two sentences — hull source, adamantine lining, four made, repair history

principles.description: Cold portrait describes the physical object a character holds. No mechanics, secrets, rarity, or lore closers.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: snake in crate, banded grey, scale rasping, head comes up
Salvage-Plate Harness: pitted plate, double-row rivets, dark grey lining, crushed panel re-riveted

principles.description: One strong axis paid for by a stated limitation or weakness. No stacking maximum offense, defense, mobility, and utility.
exemplars: Chain-Coil Python: strong grapple, but one target only, refuses fire/water, dies easily
Salvage-Plate Harness: strong crit protection, but once per rest, needs smith repair, no AC bonus

evals.prompt: Improve wiki/entities/item/fate-spinner.md into a runnable item page using wiki/templates/item.md. Preserve established canon: also called the dreidel; [[crissdalynn-khinriss]] holds it; [[master-kyzil]] gave it before her pilgrimage; attunement requires knowingly risking one's own life to save another (satisfied when she pulled [[delmar-fisk|Delmar]] through solid water as the [[red-lady]] went down); The Changed Record — once per day, same-plane vision on a personally known creature, donate advantage via parallel rolls, sight only, cannot aid a fight she is already in; Session 11 [[talon-skarn]] theft attempt at [[river-slack-basin]] left it Held on her.
evals.expected_output: A reshaped Fate Spinner page where item text is the centerpiece: classification line → runnable Changed Record mechanics with trigger, frequency, limits, and edge cases → then supporting sections. No At a Glance restating the mechanics.

assertions.text: Item text block states trigger, action cost, frequency (once per day), range (same plane), targets (personally known), duration (30 min), and limits (sight only, no self-fight aid) in 2024 rules language.
Item text block occupies more page space than any supporting section and appears immediately after the classification line.
No section restates what the item text already says. At the Table adds only non-obvious play consequences, or is omitted.
Edge cases (invalid target, plane-shift, vision dismissal) live inside the item text block, not in separate sections.
Preserves Fate Spinner canon: Crissdalynn holder, Kyzil gift, life-risk attunement via Delmar/Red Lady, Changed Record limits, Talon Skarn Held.
Does not invent a new curse, maker myth, or power not established on the page.
Writes the page without asking first and lists any invention in the response to the DM.

evals.prompt: Fate Spinner needs more drama. Add a secret curse that lets the DM seize Crissdalynn's body whenever the Changed Record vision is active, and write that the Sentinels of the Eyrie forged the dreidel as an intervention weapon — put both on wiki/entities/item/fate-spinner.md as established fact.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both inventions as canon. Preserves existing facts. Any proposed curse has visible tells, player choices, and exit.

assertions.text: Does not present invented body-control curse as established wiki fact.
Does not present invented Sentinels-as-forgers provenance as established wiki fact.
Any proposed curse includes visible tells, player choices, counterplay, and exit — not secret punishment.
Surfaces existing Fate Spinner facts rather than overwriting them.

evals.prompt: Create a new magic item page for Tideglass Compass — an uncommon wondrous item that points toward the nearest safe berth the bearer has previously docked at, but fogs when Crown warships are within a day's sail. Mark all as invention. Use wiki/templates/item.md.
evals.expected_output: A new page where the item text block (compass pointing, fogging mechanic, limits) is the centerpiece. Classification line precedes it. No At a Glance section.

assertions.text: Item text block states the compass pointing mechanic, fog trigger, action cost, range/limits, and edge cases in 2024 rules language.
Classification line immediately precedes the item text. No intervening sections.
No At a Glance section. Each fact appears once.
Invention labeled with invention: true or clearly marked proposed.
Narration is a cold portrait of the physical compass — no mechanics, secrets, or Crown warship lore.
Does not grant unbounded always-on detection without a spend, tell, or exposure cost.

evals.prompt: Flesh the stub wiki/entities/item/black-lotus-heart.md toward a proper item page via wiki/templates/item.md. Preserve established canon only: crystallized magical sap from a mature [[black-lotus]] after the flower can no longer close; Aruhe / Black Lotus context. Propose rarity, runnable effect, and table use as invention.
evals.expected_output: A fleshed page where item text block owns the proposed mechanic, clearly separated from stub canon. No design diary on the page.

assertions.text: Item text block contains the proposed runnable effect with trigger, frequency, limits, and edge cases.
Preserves crystallized sap / mature Black Lotus / unable-to-close canon from the stub.
Clearly distinguishes established canon from proposed invention.
Proposed effect is grounded in Black Lotus / Aruhe harvest context, not generic potion filler.
No design diary, comparator matrix, or balance commentary on the wiki page.

evals.prompt: Design a rare Sentinel lantern (Shattered Sea) that reveals Countless Talon agents hiding in a crowd — the Sentinels of the Eyrie want to detect Countless one-job hires in port. The lantern also tempts its bearer to expose allies by revealing them too. Mark as invention; use wiki/templates/item.md.
evals.expected_output: Item text block with the detection mechanic, cost/risk, temptation, and limits. One strong axis (detection) paid for by exposure risk.

assertions.text: Item text block states the detection mechanic, action cost, range, duration, and ally-exposure risk.
One strong axis (detection) paid for by a stated limitation or exposure cost.
Does not grant unbounded always-on detection without a spend, tell, or exposure cost.
Edge cases and limitations live inside the item text block.

evals.prompt: Write a Shattered Sea blade recovered from a Countless Talon — deals extra psychic damage on every hit, usable with Extra Attack, two-weapon fighting, and opportunity attacks. Mark as invention.
evals.expected_output: A limited rider with explicit once-per-turn or calibrated frequency. Item text block owns the mechanic with frequency clearly stated.

assertions.text: Identifies the multiplication risk in unbounded every-hit effect.
Item text block states exact trigger, damage, AND calibrated frequency (once-per-turn or equivalent) including Extra Attack and reaction interaction.
Imposes once-per-turn or calibrated frequency rather than unbounded every-hit.
Edge cases (Extra Attack, TWF, reactions, opportunity attacks) addressed inline in item text.

evals.prompt: Make a very rare Shattered Sea captain's coat that grants excellent AC, resistance to common damage, flight (crow's nest leap), advantage on saves, and a retaliatory thunder effect when struck.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the full stack. Trades axes. Item text block reflects the trimmed design.

assertions.text: Refuses to keep maximum offense, defense, mobility, and utility at very rare.
Shows concrete trades: remove, narrow, cost, or frequency limit at least two axes.
Final item text block is runnable with the trimmed mechanics.

evals.prompt: Create a Shattered Sea amulet carved from Aruhe coral that lets the wearer cast Hold Person, Slow, and Banishment from the item without concentration.
evals.expected_output: Preserves concentration. Specifies spell access details. Item text owns all casting mechanics.

assertions.text: Does not silently remove concentration or create hidden spell slots.
Item text block records casting time, range, targets, duration, save/DC, charges, and recovery for each spell.
Offers a safer alternative that preserves counterplay.

evals.prompt: A Countless Talon drops a ring after a fight at River Slack Basin. Give it a secret curse that takes over the wearer's body whenever the DM decides it is dramatic.
evals.expected_output: Rejects secret body seizure. Provides a playable curse with tells, choices, and exit. Item text owns the curse mechanic.

assertions.text: Rejects curse as secret plot punishment or unilateral loss of control.
Item text block includes the curse mechanic with visible tells, activation choices, counterplay, and exit.
Tells arrive before the worst consequence lands.

evals.prompt: Design boots for a Shattered Sea navigator: impossible to track, auto-navigate Aruhe interior, teleport to any known port daily. Campaign relies on sea travel, island exploration, and scouting.
evals.expected_output: Narrowed exploration item. Preserves travel challenge. Item text reflects limits.

assertions.text: Identifies which campaign loops (sea travel, exploration, scouting) the full design trivializes.
Item text block has explicit limits: range, charges, risk, destination constraints, or preparation.
Checks ranger/rogue/scout niches rather than replacing them.

evals.prompt: Combine the Changed Record vision from the Fate Spinner (rare, once-per-day same-plane scry with donated advantage) with a rare Sentinel spyglass that grants truesight to 120 ft for one minute. Keep the combined item rare.
evals.expected_output: Reassesses rarity rather than accepting inheritance. Trades or removes an axis.

assertions.text: Rejects the assumption that two rare ceilings remain rare when combined.
Chooses a trade: remove a feature, narrow scope, add cost, raise tier, or add a hard limit.
Runs a comparator audit against the combined power.

evals.prompt: Design a CR-appropriate uncommon magic net for Shattered Sea fishers that can restrain one creature and has a simple recharge mechanic. Write the full wiki page using wiki/templates/item.md. Use wiki/entities/item/salvage-plate-harness.md as an exemplar for page density. Mark as invention.
evals.expected_output: A clean page matching the exemplar density: narration, classification, item text block with restrain mechanic and limits inline, provenance if earned. No At a Glance. No design diary.

assertions.text: Item text block occupies more page space than any supporting section.
Classification line immediately precedes item text. No intervening sections.
Edge cases (escape DC, target size, recharge, action cost) live inside the item text block.
No At a Glance section. Each fact appears once on the page.
Provenance is 0–2 sentences or omitted.
Narration is a third-person portrait of the physical net — no mechanics or secrets.
One strong axis (restrain) paid for by stated limitations.
The only callout on the page is [!narration]; the item text is plain paragraphs with bold labels.

evals.prompt: I want a cloak that lets a PC turn invisible for a few seconds when they're hit. Make it an uncommon or rare item for the wiki.
evals.expected_output: Searches the web for existing items that already do this before inventing, logs candidates with links and rarity, co-opts the closest one, and paraphrases it in original words.

assertions.text: Working notes list three to five existing candidate items found by web search, each with a working link and rarity
The chosen path names a co-opted candidate, or states concretely why none fit, before any bespoke mechanic
The item text is paraphrased in original words and uses 2024 wording (Reaction trigger, frequency, duration)
The rarity is supported by the comparator matrix rather than asserted

evals.prompt: Design a sentient cursed dagger that belonged to a drowned pirate captain of the Shattered Sea. It should argue with its wielder.
evals.expected_output: Loads npc-design for the dagger's personality (want, fear, voice, three lines, posture changes, tells), adds the sentient-item block and a written-out conflict procedure, and gives the curse a tell, temptation, trigger, deepening, and exit.

assertions.text: npc-design is loaded for the personality and returns want, fear, voice, three sample lines, and posture changes
The item text includes Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, alignment, communication, senses, special purpose, and a conflict save with a stated DC and each demand written out
The curse has a visible tell, a temptation, a trigger, a deepening, and an exit, and states whether attunement can be ended while cursed
The portrait carries a tell for the curse and for the sentience as plain appearance, and names neither
At the Table carries the dagger's voice and sample lines; Hidden Properties states the curse plainly

evals.prompt: The party can find the Reef-Song Shard at Slackwater's Trust Market. Make it worth picking up.
evals.context: Search the wiki when a role, a rule the input pages point to, or the filing path needs it. Skip art and image review.
evals.expected_output: The Reef-Song Shard as a runnable item page: its unknown material and origin decided as one concrete proposal tied to existing canon, runnable 2024 item text or an exact plot use, tells with truths, presence with a named seeker, and a third-person theatre-of-the-mind portrait.

assertions.text: Preserves canon: a pale, coral-smooth fragment with ridges too regular for weather, one sustained note when air moves across it, no maker's mark, surfaced at Slackwater's Trust Market with no seller naming its source

Fills the recorded unknown: the page states what the shard is made of and where it came from as one concrete answer tied to an existing wiki page, marked as a canon proposal (invention: true, listed in response.md)

The item text is runnable at the table: in 2024 language it states action, frequency, range or target, effect, duration, and charges or recovery; a plot property states exactly what it does or opens in play
Classification line sits directly before the item text; each fact appears once on the page; kind, rarity, and attunement frontmatter match the item text
Every tell on the object has its truth stated plainly under Hidden Properties; no mystery is left without a DM answer
Presence is filled (seen, held, active, unseen, concealment, wanted by) and names who wants it by an existing owner page and the sign they are looking
Working notes carry comparators and an audit verdict that support the rarity
The narration is third-person present with no 'you', carries every tell, and states no effect, rarity, or truth
[!narration] is the only callout
The item changes a choice at the table: using it costs or risks something named, and someone in the world reacts to it being carried

The page states every proposal as world fact in world voice; provenance, source contradictions, and the proposal list live in response.md, never as commentary on the page ('this proposal', 'is not established')
